the A137 commit guard REFUSED its first real commit: the 3c amendment was blocked on suite_exit=1 with two browser tests (test_browser_review_board_references: test_duplicate_filenames_both_display, test_groups_render_in_fixed_order_with_owner_labels) failing in a full run. Isolated re-run 12/12 passed; a single pre-committed full re-run passed 4318. The failure is NON-DETERMINISTIC and recorded OPEN, not resolved — cause not established (StaticLiveServerTestCase binds a random port, so the live runserver is not a collision; the documented shared-test-DB ordering flake is a hypothesis, not a finding). The guard did the job it was built for: a red suite could not become a commit

the A183 migration's cosmetic claim was TRUE but its proof established a weaker proposition: a per-symbol distribution invariant cannot see an in-place edit, and the gap was filled by a fact the author knew and the instrument never checked. Replaced by the raw-match-text multiset (which subsumes the distribution) plus a git assertion that the migration commit touched no scanned source; re-run against f10d2a2 — ESTABLISHED; both halves demonstrated REFUTABLE by negative control, so the verification is evidence rather than a tautology

STANDING RULE: a sweep reports its own enumeration boundary as data — what it searched, what it could not reach, and why — before it reports findings. Written because a sweep called four entries 'era unavailable' when they sat in a subdirectory: the instrument's boundary read as a property of the world, the third instance of that shape alongside the A184 collapse and pipeline_errors.py:76

the pre-committed re-run is legitimate exactly once per registered flake; invoked twice it is run-it-until-green with a declaration stapled on, which looks governed and is therefore worse than an ungoverned retry. Bound MECHANICALLY: tools/flake_gate.py runs inside the commit guard, consumes the invocation in the register, and STOPS the node on a second occurrence; an unregistered failure is reported as a finding, never a retry
